title: The Saga of Milli Vanilli
summary: Hosts Josh and Chuck tell the story of Milli Vanilli, the German-produced pop duo whose lead vocals were performed by session singers. They cover producer Frank Farian's background and earlier group Boney M., the theft of the song "Girl You Know It's True" from New Mark's, the recruitment of Rob Pilatus and Fab Morvan, the lip-syncing deception, the group's US rise on Arista, the Bristol, Connecticut concert malfunction, the 1990 Grammy award that was revoked, Farian's confession, the class action settlement, the duo's later solo album, Rob Pilatus's death in 1998, and an upcoming biopic. Listener mail from Maggie closes the episode about her husband falling asleep at a Boston show.
topics: Stuff You Should Know listener mail

segments.title: Opening banter
segments.summary: Hosts introduce the Milli Vanilli episode and note the US Army's role and how the story is more complex than the fraud label suggests.

segments.title: Frank Farian and Boney M.
segments.summary: Background on producer Frank Farian, his blue-eyed soul ambitions, his production career, and the Boney M. model in which he sang while other performers appeared as the group; Bobby Farrell's vocals were re-recorded.

segments.title: Theft of Girl You Know It's True
segments.summary: Farian took the song Girl You Know It's True, originally recorded by New Mark's with singers from StarPoint and others, and remade it nearly identically; the original sold about eight thousand records.

segments.title: Rob Pilatus and Fab Morvan backgrounds
segments.summary: Biographies of Fab Morvan, a former gymnast turned dancer, and Rob Pilatus, a breakdancer and model, and how they met in 1984.

segments.title: Meeting Farian and the contract
segments.summary: Farian contacted Pilatus and Morvan on New Year's Day 1988, played them the song, and they signed a contract believing they would sing; Farian had already decided they would only lip sync.

segments.title: Hidden session singers
segments.summary: The actual vocals were recorded by Brad Howell, John Davis and rapper Charles Shaw; the duo were presented as the group. The name Milli Vanilli's origin is disputed.

segments.title: Name origin and 80s music aside
segments.summary: Hosts discuss theories about the name Milli Vanilli and digress into favorite 1980s songs.

segments.title: Early European suspicion
segments.summary: The song became a hit in Germany; Charles Shaw went public and was reportedly silenced; a European DJ asked them to sing live; their accents and limited English raised doubts.

segments.title: Golden prison and advances
segments.summary: Pilatus and Morvan kept asking to sing but were financially bound by large advances and the contract.

segments.title: US release and chart success
segments.summary: Arista signed them in 1989; Girl You Know It's True was released as a single and album, selling about eleven million copies worldwide, with a string of number one and top five hits.
topics: Girl You Know It's True album

segments.title: Move to Beverly Hills and management
segments.summary: The duo relocated to Beverly Hills in June 1989 and signed with manager Sandy Gallen, who also managed Dolly Parton; they joined the first Club MTV tour.

segments.title: Interviews stop and Super Mario cartoon
segments.summary: After US radio and TV interviews stopped, they voiced themselves in a Super Mario Bros. 3 cartoon and a flat a cappella clip circulated.

segments.title: Bristol, Connecticut concert malfunction
segments.summary: At a July 1989 concert in Bristol, Connecticut, the backing track skipped; Pilatus ran off stage and Julie Brown persuaded him to return. The duo later called it the beginning of the end.

segments.title: Critics and the Elvis quote
segments.summary: Critics treated the act as a symbol of shallow pop; the hosts discuss the duo's own contribution, the 107-city tour, and Pilatus's controversial quotes comparing them to Bob Dylan and Elvis.

segments.title: Press tour and planned medley
segments.summary: After the controversial quotes, the label and managers planned a press tour and a medley of Beatles, Rolling Stones and Bob Dylan songs, which the duo rejected.

segments.title: Who knew what
segments.summary: The hosts discuss who in the industry knew about the lip syncing; Todd Headley said everyone connected knew, while Arista publicly denied knowledge, though letters from lawyers reached Clive Davis.

segments.title: 1990 Grammy and revocation
segments.summary: Milli Vanilli won Best New Artist at the 1990 Grammys and performed lip synced; the award was revoked, and no Best New Artist award was given that year. At a press conference, a voice coach claimed they could sing.

segments.title: Farian confesses
segments.summary: Five days before the Grammys, Frank Farian publicly disclosed the deception; Arista's Roy Lott's comment about sales was discussed.

segments.title: Wider impact and other lip sync cases
segments.summary: The scandal fueled broader criticism of manufactured pop; Martha Wash's vocals on The Real Thing hit were used without her knowledge, and Village People rumors were discussed.

segments.title: Class action settlement
segments.summary: Fans filed class action lawsuits; the settlement offered up to three dollars per claimant from BMG and Arista; the hosts discuss whether the fraud mattered.

segments.title: Rob and Fab solo album
segments.summary: Pilatus and Morvan released a solo album using their real voices, which flopped, selling about two thousand copies in the US, released in 1993 and performed live on the Arsenio Hall Show.

segments.title: Rob Pilatus death and later life
segments.summary: Pilatus struggled with addiction and was found dead in a hotel room in April 1998 from an accidental overdose; Morvan later toured with John Davis as Face Meets Voice.

segments.title: Biopic
segments.summary: A Milli Vanilli biopic is in production with actors in costume, with the 300 Entertainment CEO credited as executive producer.

segments.title: Reaction videos and wrap-up
segments.summary: The hosts mention a YouTube reaction video to Girl You Know It's True and close the topic discussion.

segments.title: Listener mail: husband falls asleep at Boston show
segments.summary: Maggie writes that her husband dozed off during the Boston live show; hosts respond.

segments.title: Sign-off
segments.summary: Hosts give the email address and credits iHeartRadio.
